source.title: Rethinking trauma-related psychopathology in the Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP)

confidence_rationale: Argues for explicitly DISAGGREGATING psychopathology symptoms from their purported causes -- maintaining a taxonomy of causal/etiological events (e.g. trauma type, duration, subjective meaning) separately from the symptom-dimension taxonomy. This is the cleanest literature statement of Q-064's predisposition/expression-factoring requirement (keep 'which axes are fragile / what perturbed them' distinct from 'which failure mode is expressed'). Moderate confidence: it is a focused conceptual argument within one symptom domain (trauma), not a general empirical validation, and it concerns external causes rather than internal vulnerability axes per se.
failure_signatures: Folding cause into the symptom representation (as PTSD does by building the stressor into the diagnosis) produces within-category heterogeneity and excessive comorbidity -- the failure Q-064 avoids by keeping predisposition/perturbation separate from expressed syndrome; collapsing them is the named anti-pattern.

Different features of the same perturbation (type, duration, subjective meaning) yield different symptom sequelae across spectra, so a single predisposition state can map to many expressions -- supports the separation but warns the predisposition->expression map is high-dimensional and context-gated, not one-to-one.

mapping.source_claim_statement: HiTOP's symptom-covariation focus leaves a gap for trauma-related psychopathology because predominant definitions (e.g. PTSD) build the purported cause into the symptom category, creating content-coverage problems, within-category heterogeneity, and excessive comorbidity; the authors argue for disaggregating symptoms from causes -- developing a detailed taxonomy of traumatic EVENTS alongside the evolving HiTOP symptom model -- so that different features of a traumatic experience can be linked to different symptom sequelae across spectra.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-064 requires that axis-PREDISPOSITION (which mechanisms are fragile / what perturbed them) be kept separable from axis-EXPRESSION (which failure mode is realized, gated by developmental/plasticity machinery). This paper makes the same architectural argument in the trauma domain: keep the causal/perturbation taxonomy separate from the symptom-dimension taxonomy, because a given perturbation can express across multiple symptom dimensions. It is a worked precedent for the two-layer factoring Q-064 needs.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper concerns EXTERNAL causes (traumatic events) rather than internal latent VULNERABILITY axes, and is confined to the trauma-related corner of psychopathology; the cause/symptom disaggregation is a strong analogy for Q-064's predisposition/expression split but is not the same distinction, and it is argued, not empirically demonstrated, here.
mapping.source_context: Conceptual review / position piece on situating trauma-related psychopathology within the HiTOP dimensional framework.

confidence_components.notes: Well-argued position piece in a reputable specialty journal (source_quality moderate -- conceptual, single-domain). Mapping_fidelity moderate: the disaggregate-cause-from-symptom argument is a close analogue of Q-064's predisposition/expression factoring, but addresses external events rather than internal vulnerability axes. Transfer risk moderate-high for the same reason.
